forcedChoices.reason: Spanish needs ser or estar; 'estar en acto' and 'estar en potencia' are the standard phrases and avoid the false friend 'actual'.

forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces the gender of 'orden'; the feminine (an order of beings) and a singular verb keep the subject of the English.

forcedChoices.choice: entre el potencial y el acto
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish 'lo actual' means 'the current'; 'el acto' carries the sense of the glossary term.

forcedChoices.choice: al experimentar, los Ajustadores son como el Supremo
forcedChoices.reason: English 'as' can mean 'while' or 'because'; the infinitive construction keeps both readings open.
Spanish 'paternidad' would fix a male sense; the text later calls the Supreme 'Mother', so a sex-neutral form keeps the English open.
Spanish has no plain pair for 'son' and 'child' here; 'hijo' fits both without adding a sense.
